artifacts.notes: Folios v r - vi v of Dominica prima adventus. PDF page 1 = position 31 (f. v r): only the right column from Deinde dicat presbiter in silentio is in the constituent. Pages 2-3 = positions 32-33 are wholly inside it. Page 4 = position 34 (f. vi v): only the left column through the Amen after Per omnia secula seculorum is inside. On position 32 the marginal Forma ista note, the fraction figure and the Roman consecration form below the columns appear to be printed on separate pasted slips (visual impression only, not established). Position 33 carries a manuscript interlinear et between patre and filio in the creed, excluded as a copy-specific annotation. Identity: the separately retained original colophon (position 965) and its publication-date passage.

passages.locus: Benedictio panis: blessing
passages.notes: Independent page-collated reading transcription, not OCR. Expand printed contractions; long-s to s; consonantal u/v and i/j standardized; et replaces ampersand or Tironian et; ae ligatures expanded as ae. Preserve the 1500 e spellings celum, anime, seculum and presbiter, versus 1804 caelum, animae, saeculum and presbyter. Case and punctuation regularized; 1804 printed acute accents are omitted, and æ is expanded as ae. Preserve every lexical item, response and rubric, all three crosses including San✠cti, and Amens. The 1500 terram uses final-m abbreviation. The original orthographic differences are visible, not classified as liturgical revision.

passages.locus: Ordo missae (Dominica prima de adventu): accipiat-corpus-rubrica; retained facsimile page(s) 2-3
passages.notes: Independent page-image reading transcription, not OCR; OCR and Migne PL 85 used only as leads. Expand printed contractions and suspensions; long-s to s; consonantal u/v and i/j standardized; et replaces ampersand or Tironian et; ae and oe ligatures expanded as ae and oe; the printed accents of 1755 and 1804 omitted. Case and clause punctuation regularized: all three Ordo readings use the 1500 pointing and capitalization for corresponding wording, with nomina sacra capitalized; printed commas, semicolons and line layout are not recorded. The word-dividing colons of the consecration words and of the Roman form printed below them are recorded exactly as each edition prints them (present in 1500 and 1755, absent in 1804). Preserve every lexical item, edition spelling (for example celum/caelum, presbiter/presbyter, simbolum/symbolum, cenavit/coenavit, annunciabitis/annuntiabitis, temptationem/tentationem), response, rubric and printed cross at its printed position, including crosses inside words. No conjectural restoration: the 1500 sancti✠cas, meremur and ad dextera are kept as printed. The fraction figure's nine labels are serialized in the order that 1804 numbers 1-9 (column top to bottom, left arm, right arm, then the two right-hand labels); 1500 and 1755 print no numbers. Where the figure interrupts a unit, the figure is serialized after that unit. Running heads, folio, page, column and editorial line numbers, signatures, catchwords and manuscript annotations are excluded.

work.author: Archdiocese of Toledo
work.description: The altar book of the Hispano-Mozarabic rite -- the old Spanish rite, the Visigothic and Isidorian use of the peninsula, suppressed for the Roman use in the eleventh century and kept alive at Toledo, where Cardinal Ximenez de Cisneros endowed the chapel of Corpus Christi in the cathedral for its celebration and had the Missale mixtum printed in 1500. IT IS NOT THE MISSALE ROMANUM AND MUST NOT BE FILED WITH IT: its Mass has its own shape, with the Illatio for the Preface, the Post pridie for what the Roman book puts after the institution narrative, the fraction of the Host into nine particles, and the Creed said after the consecration. It is registered under the archdiocese of Toledo because Toledo is the church whose ordinary has held and legislated for the rite continuously -- Cisneros for the 1500 printing, Lorenzana for the 1770s recension that Migne reprints -- on the same pattern as work.archdiocese-of-braga.missale-bracarense. NEITHER EDITION REGISTERED HERE IS A TYPICAL EDITION AND NEITHER IS AN ACT. Both are scholarly reprintings of the Cisneros book: Alexander Lesley's of 1755, printed at Rome with his own preface, notes and appendix, and Migne's of 1862, which reprints Lesley in the Patrologia Latina. The rite's own modern book, the Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum promulgated at Toledo in 1991 and 1994, is in copyright, was not acquired, and has no record here.
